p5_b4.ocr: Change rates in ontology evolution Most ontologies in life science evolve continuously to account for new discoveries [11, 13, 14]. Our experimental studies indicated that the change rates of redundant is- a relations are significantly higher than the change rates of all is-a relations for both SNOMED CT and Gene Ontology. Figure 4 is a graphical summary of the differences between SNOMED CT versions using the change rate of redundant is-a relations versus the change rate of all is-a relations. The change rate between two versions is defined as (|N − O| + |O − N|)/(|O| + |N|), where
